name: Alaska
rule: We did not read Alaska's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Arizona
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, with the employee's prior written authorization, or where there is a reasonable good faith dispute over the amount due (including a set-off the employer claims).

name: Colorado
rule: CDLE allows 10 days to audit that property or money entrusted to the employee was returned; written notice and other requirements apply to deductions in that case. Other deduction rules were not read.

name: Connecticut
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, or with the employee's written authorization on a form approved by the labor commissioner (plus medical deductions without financial benefit to the employer, and automatic retirement enrollment).

name: Delaware
rule: Only if required or empowered by law, for medical care without financial benefit to the employer, or with a signed authorization for a lawful purpose that benefits the employee.

name: District of Columbia
rule: We did not read District of Columbia's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Idaho
rule: Allowed: with proof of the advance or draw, the full amount can be withheld.

name: Illinois
verdict: only if the advance agreement provided for it
rule: Allowed from final compensation only if the agreement signed when the advance was made provided for it.

name: Iowa
rule: Only if required or permitted by law or a court, or with written authorization for a lawful purpose that benefits the employee. Some items can never be deducted (shared-till shortages, most breakage and damage, lost or stolen property unless it was assigned equipment the employee acknowledged in writing).

name: Kansas
rule: Allowed from final wages after a written notice and explanation (a loan or advance made during and within the scope of employment).

name: Maine
rule: Allowed if the loan or advance is evidenced by a statement in writing signed by the employee.

name: Maryland
rule: Only if ordered by a court, authorized expressly in writing by the employee, allowed by the Commissioner because the employee received full consideration, or made under another law.

name: Minnesota
verdict: allowed if authorized in writing before the loan
rule: A purchase or loan may be deducted, including at termination, if the employee authorized it in writing before making it; otherwise only with written authorization after the debt arose.

name: Montana
rule: Reasonable deductions for board, room and other incidentals that are a condition of employment, or as otherwise provided by law. When an employee is discharged over an alleged theft connected to the work, the employer may withhold the value of the theft from the final paycheck if the conditions of 39-3-205(3) are met.

name: New Jersey
verdict: only on the original loan schedule
rule: An employer loan may be repaid only on the periodic schedule in the original loan agreement.

name: New York
rule: We did not read New York's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: North Carolina
rule: With a written authorization signed on or before the payday that gives the reason and the dollar amount or percentage; if the amount is not known in advance, a written authorization with the reason, then written notice of the amount and of the right to withdraw. Deductions for the employer's benefit may not cut into minimum wage or overtime.

name: North Dakota
rule: Allowed: advances paid to employees, other than undocumented cash.

name: Oklahoma
rule: We did not read Oklahoma's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: Oregon
rule: Only if legally required, or the employee voluntarily agrees in writing and the deduction is for the employee's benefit.

name: Pennsylvania
rule: We did not read Pennsylvania's deduction rule on its own sites, so only the federal floor below applies here.

name: South Carolina
rule: Only if required or permitted by law, or the employer gave the written notice of the deductions required at hiring (with seven days' written notice of changes).

name: South Dakota
rule: The employer may withhold the final paycheck until the employee returns property that belongs to the employer.

name: Tennessee
rule: Generally no deductions without the employee's consent in a signed written agreement.

name: Texas
rule: Only if ordered by a court, authorized by law, or with the employee's written authorization for a lawful purpose.

name: Vermont
rule: Allowed deductions are set by Vermont's Minimum Wage Rules (not read here); the department stresses that the employee must still receive at least minimum wage.

name: Virginia
rule: Only taxes, deductions in accordance with law, or with the employee's written and signed authorization.

name: Washington
rule: Only if required by law, specifically agreed orally or in writing by the employee and employer (except as RCW 49.48.160 prohibits), or for medical care recorded in the books.

name: West Virginia
rule: Deductions are amounts required by law and authorized amounts for dues, pensions, savings, credit unions, charities and insurance. Unreturned employer property over $100 can be deducted from final wages at its replacement cost only under a signed itemized agreement and a written notice and demand.

name: Wyoming
rule: Deductions are allowed in certain cases, including cash shortages, repayment of loans or advances, and damaged or lost equipment, and must follow the wage offset rules (not read here).
